subproblems.title: Support of a current that vanishes on forms supported away from a compact set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open, let K ⊆ U be compact, and let F be an n-current in U (GeometricCurrentOn U n) such that F(ω) = 0 for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n) whose topological support is disjoint from K. Then spt F ⊆ K and spt F is compact. Here spt F = U ∖ Z(F) (GeometricCurrentOn.support, Simon 6.2.11), where the zero region Z(F) is the union of all open sets W with closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U K : Set (Euclid P)) (F : GeometricCurrentOn U n), IsOpen U → IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, Disjoint (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) K → F ω = 0) → F.support ⊆ K ∧ IsCompact F.support
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 2 and 4 of the selected proof of cmcdtfrbv_boundary_support_subset_faces. There a ball around a point off the compact set Z has compact closure and the current vanishes on it, so the ball lies in the zero region. Here this is stated for an arbitrary open domain U, compact K ⊆ U and current F (Simon 6.2.11, book/chapter-06.txt lines 296–301). This is exactly the frozen type of the accepted declaration rsd_cmr_support_subset_of_vanish, which is reused unchanged. The selected proof applies it with U = ℝ^P, n = m, K = Z and F = ∂Q₀.

Definitions (SimonGMT, CurrentLocalEquality.lean). F vanishes on W (GeometricCurrentOn.VanishesOn) if F(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Z(F) := zeroRegion F is the union of all W with W open, closure(W) compact, closure(W) ⊆ U and F vanishing on W. spt F := support F = U ∖ Z(F).

1. No point of U ∖ K lies in spt F. Let y ∈ U ∖ K. K is compact, hence closed in the Hausdorff space ℝ^P (IsCompact.isClosed), and U is open, so U ∖ K is open (IsOpen.sdiff). By Metric.isOpen_iff there is s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Put W := B_{s/2}(y).
 (a) W is open (isOpen_ball), and y ∈ W because s/2 > 0 (mem_ball_self).
 (b) closure(W) ⊆ B̄_{s/2}(y) (closure_ball_subset_closedBall) ⊆ B_s(y) (because s/2 < s) ⊆ U ∖ K ⊆ U.
 (c) closure(W) is compact. It is a closed subset (isClosed_closure) of B̄_{s/2}(y), and that closed ball is compact because ℝ^P is a proper space (isCompact_closedBall); apply IsCompact.of_isClosed_subset.
 (d) F vanishes on W. Let ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then tsupport ω ⊆ W ⊆ B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K, so tsupport ω is disjoint from K, and F(ω) = 0 by hypothesis.
 By (a)–(d), W is one of the sets whose union is Z(F). Since y ∈ W, y ∈ Z(F), so y ∉ spt F.
2. spt F ⊆ K. Let x ∈ spt F = U ∖ Z(F). Then x ∈ U. If x ∉ K, then x ∈ U ∖ K and step 1 gives x ∉ spt F, a contradiction. Hence x ∈ K.
3. spt F is compact. We have spt F = K ∖ Z(F). If x ∈ spt F, then x ∈ K by step 2 and x ∉ Z(F). If x ∈ K ∖ Z(F), then x ∈ U because K ⊆ U, so x ∈ U ∖ Z(F) = spt F. Z(F) is open as a union of open sets (GeometricCurrentOn.isOpen_zeroRegion). The difference of a compact set and an open set is compact (IsCompact.diff), so K ∖ Z(F) = spt F is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: For y ∈ U ∖ K choose s > 0 with B_s(y) ⊆ U ∖ K. Then W := B_{s/2}(y) is open, contains y, and its compact closure lies in U ∖ K ⊆ U.
Every test form supported in W has support disjoint from K, so F vanishes on W. Hence y ∈ Z(F) and y ∉ spt F.
Therefore spt F = U ∖ Z(F) ⊆ K.
spt F = K ∖ Z(F), with K compact and Z(F) open, is compact.

subproblems.title: The union of the closed faces Φ_q([0,1]^{m+1}), q ∈ s, is compact
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let s be a finite set of index pairs q = (ι, b) with ι : Fin (m+1) → Fin P and b : Fin P → ℤ. For q = (ι, b) and y ∈ Euclid (m+1) put Φ_q(y) := b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} ∈ ℝ^P. Here b is regarded as the vector WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ)) and e_l := EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Then Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : x = Φ_q(y) for some q ∈ s and some y ∈ Euclid (m+1) with 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i} is compact.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))), IsCompact {x : Euclid P | ∃ q ∈ s, ∃ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = x}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the selected proof of cmcdtfrbv_boundary_support_subset_faces (Z := ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(Cⁿ) is compact).

Notation. C := {y ∈ Euclid (m+1) : 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i} is the closed unit cube.

1. C is closed. By set extensionality, C = ⋂_i ({y : 0 ≤ y_i} ∩ {y : y_i ≤ 1}). Each coordinate map y ↦ y_i on Euclid (m+1) is continuous (fun_prop). Comparing it with a constant, {y : 0 ≤ y_i} and {y : y_i ≤ 1} are closed (isClosed_le with continuous_const). Their intersection is closed (IsClosed.inter), and so is the intersection over all i (isClosed_iInter).
2. C is bounded. Let y ∈ C. For every i, 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 gives |y_i|² = y_i·y_i ≤ 1·1 = 1. Hence ‖y‖ = √(Σ_i |y_i|²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq) ≤ √(Σ_i 1) = √(m+1) (Finset.sum_le_sum and Real.sqrt_le_sqrt). So C ⊆ closedBall(0, √(m+1)), and C is bounded (Metric.isBounded_iff_subset_closedBall).
3. C is compact. Euclid (m+1) is a finite-dimensional real normed space, hence a proper metric space, and a closed bounded subset of a proper space is compact (Metric.isCompact_of_isClosed_isBounded, applied to steps 1 and 2).
4. Each Φ_q(C) is compact. Φ_q(y) = b + Σ_j y_j • e_{ι(j)} is a constant vector plus a finite sum of the maps y ↦ y_j • e_{ι(j)}. Each of these is a continuous coordinate times a constant vector. Constants, finite sums and scalar multiples of continuous maps are continuous (fun_prop), so Φ_q is continuous. The continuous image of a compact set is compact (IsCompact.image), so Φ_q(C) is compact.
5. Z = ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(C). By definition, x ∈ Z iff there are q ∈ s and y ∈ C with Φ_q(y) = x. That holds iff x ∈ Φ_q(C) for some q ∈ s (set extensionality with mem_iUnion and mem_image).
6. A union of compact sets indexed by the finite set s is compact (Finset.isCompact_biUnion). By steps 4 and 5, Z is compact. ∎
proof_key_steps: The closed unit cube C ⊆ Euclid (m+1) is closed, as an intersection of coordinate half-spaces, and bounded, since ‖y‖ ≤ √(m+1). Hence it is compact.
Each affine map Φ_q is continuous, so Φ_q(C) is compact.
Z = ⋃_{q∈s} Φ_q(C) is a finite union of compact sets, hence compact.

subproblems.title: ∂Q₀ annihilates test forms whose support misses the closed faces
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and n := m + 1. Let s be a finite set of index pairs p = (ι, b) with ι : Fin n → Fin P and b : Fin P → ℤ, and let u_p : Euclid n → ℝ be arbitrary functions. Let Q₀ be an n-current on ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with Q₀(ω) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y)·ω(Φ_p y)(e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}) dy for every test n-form ω. Here Q₁ = (0,1)ⁿ = {y : 0 < y_i < 1 for every i}, Φ_p(y) = b + Σ_j y_j e_{ι(j)} (b regarded as WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (b i : ℝ))) and e_l = EuclideanSpace.single l 1. Let Z := {x ∈ ℝ^P : x = Φ_q(y) for some q ∈ s and some y ∈ Euclid n with 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1 for every i}. Then ∂Q₀(γ) = 0 (Q₀.boundary γ = 0) for every test m-form γ ∈ TestFormOn univ m whose topological support is disjoint from Z.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (s : Finset ((Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ))) (u : (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P) × (Fin P → ℤ) → Euclid (m + 1) → ℝ) (Q₀ : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1)), (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) (m + 1), Q₀ ω = ∑ p ∈ s, ∫ y in {y : Euclid (m + 1) | ∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1}, u p y * (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (p.1 j) (1 : ℝ))) → ∀ γ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) m, Disjoint (tsupport (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m)) {x : Euclid P | ∃ q ∈ s, ∃ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 ≤ y i ∧ y i ≤ 1) ∧ (WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (q.2 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (q.1 j) (1 : ℝ)) = x} → Q₀.boundary γ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the selected proof of cmcdtfrbv_boundary_support_subset_faces. There the test form γ satisfies tsupport γ ⊆ W for a ball W disjoint from Z. The argument only uses that tsupport γ is disjoint from Z, which is the hypothesis here.

Notation. For p = (ι_p, b_p) ∈ s put E_p := (e_{ι_p(0)}, …, e_{ι_p(m)}). Fix a test m-form γ ∈ TestFormOn univ m with tsupport γ ∩ Z = ∅.

1. Boundary as an exterior derivative. By definition of the boundary (GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply), ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ). Here dγ := exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m γ is the test (m+1)-form on univ whose underlying differential form is exteriorDerivative γ.
2. Support of dγ. Exterior differentiation does not enlarge the topological support (tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset), so tsupport(dγ) ⊆ tsupport γ. Hence tsupport(dγ) ∩ Z = ∅.
3. Representation. The hypothesis on Q₀, applied to the test (m+1)-form ω := dγ, gives Q₀(dγ) = Σ_{p∈s} ∫_{Q₁} u_p(y)·(dγ)(Φ_p y)(E_p) dy.
4. The integrands vanish on Q₁. Fix p ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁. For each i, 0 < y_i < 1 implies 0 ≤ y_i ≤ 1, so Φ_p(y) ∈ Z (witnesses q := p and the same y). By step 2, Φ_p(y) ∉ tsupport(dγ). A function is zero at every point outside its topological support (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so the covector (dγ)(Φ_p y) is 0. Hence (dγ)(Φ_p y)(E_p) = 0 and u_p(y)·(dγ)(Φ_p y)(E_p) = u_p(y)·0 = 0.
5. Conclusion. By step 4, for every p ∈ s the integrand is 0 at every point of Q₁, so its set integral over Q₁ is 0 (setIntegral_eq_zero_of_forall_eq_zero, which needs no integrability or measurability hypothesis). A finite sum of zeros is 0 (Finset.sum_eq_zero). By steps 1 and 3, ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ) = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: ∂Q₀(γ) = Q₀(dγ), where dγ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m γ.
tsupport dγ ⊆ tsupport γ, so tsupport dγ misses Z.
Expand Q₀(dγ) with the representation hypothesis.
For p ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁, Φ_p(y) ∈ Z, so Φ_p(y) ∉ tsupport dγ. Hence dγ(Φ_p y) = 0 and the integrand vanishes.
Every set integral is 0, so the finite sum and ∂Q₀(γ) are 0.
